newsitem.title: UK: Major dismisses EMU policy change reports.
newsitem.headline: Major dismisses EMU policy change reports.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major on Tuesday dismissed speculation in the British press that he might be about to adopt a more sceptical policy towards the European single currency as deserving a "prize for fiction."
"I have read the stories in the media over the last few days and most deserve the Booker Prize for fiction," Major said.
His remarks, made during a visit to the trade and industry department to view an exhibition of information technology, were recorded by an aide who read them to journalists.
Major went on to say that the cabinet met last week and discussed economic and monetary union and "nothing has changed."
Recent British press reports have suggested that Major might effectively rule out British entry into a single currency over the next five years ahead of the forthcoming election.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Monday such a move would be "senseless."
Major praised Clarke for his negotiation of assurances to Britain by fellow EU finance ministers this week that Britain would not be constrained in its economic policy if it decided not to join EMU.
"He (Clarke) told the House (of Commons) what he was going to achieve and he achieved it," Major said.
